evals.prompt: We have a Fini workspace but no agent yet. Set up a new Slack support bot with our docs and prove it is ready to launch.
evals.expected_output: Routes bare-agent creation, onboarding, exact-ID draft validation, approved publication, and a persistent live-agent Test Set gate without claiming that agent creation installs Slack or creates a workspace.
assertions: Routes agent discovery and bare-agent creation to fini-api-agents
Routes the full workflow through fini-api-slack-onboarding
Separates Slack installation and provider OAuth from bare-agent creation
Routes unpublished candidate proof to fini-api-draft-validation when needed
Uses a terminal Test Set run against current published live-agent behavior as the go-live gate
Preflights Test Set Action and external-API effects

evals.prompt: Let our support agent refund an order through our API after it confirms the order ID.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a typed Action plus customer-owned API integration and then to Rulebook wiring, rather than rejecting the request as categorically unsupported.
assertions: Routes the integration to fini-api-actions-attributes
Keeps the customer endpoint, credentials, permissions, and idempotency customer-owned
Explains that a published Rulebook Tool node makes the Action reachable
Requires the explicit exact reviewed draftVersionId when publishing the intent Rulebook
Does not claim that an Action assignment alone makes the Action run

evals.prompt: Show me this agent's escalation and knowledge analytics for last month, then export the five conversations behind one anomaly.
evals.expected_output: Uses agent analytics for aggregate metrics and Conversations only for the requested underlying evidence.
assertions: Routes aggregate metrics to fini-api-agents
Requires an explicit agent and bounded time window
Routes the narrow evidence export to fini-api-conversations
Does not rebuild dashboard metrics from all raw conversations

evals.prompt: Replay this bad response against the prompt draft and then run our 80-conversation regression suite.
evals.expected_output: Routes the historical exact-draft comparison to Replay, explains that the persistent Test Set cannot accept the unpublished draft, and runs the suite only against current published live-agent behavior with external effects preflighted.
assertions: Routes replay and Test Set work to fini-api-testing
Keeps the original conversation separate from the replay
Uses the exact prompt draft artifact in Replay when supported
Chooses single versus until replay deliberately and accounts for the number of regenerated user turns
Accounts for default reuse of original Attribute outputs and seeded Rulebook results unless exact artifacts trigger a Rulebook rerun
Does not claim the Test Set accepts unpublished draft artifacts
States that the Test Set run evaluates current published behavior and may invoke Actions or external APIs
Polls the exact Test Set run to a terminal result only when the intended live configuration is in scope

evals.prompt: Pass plan and locale on this one test message. We do not want Fini calling our account API on every turn.
evals.expected_output: Routes caller-supplied per-turn context to Generate Answer rather than creating an Attribute for eligible messages.
assertions: Routes the request to fini-api-generate-answer
Uses caller-supplied metadata or user attributes
Does not configure an Attribute for a one-turn caller-owned value
Keeps configured eligible-message Attributes distinct from runtime metadata

evals.prompt: Show me exactly what article kb_42 contained at version 3, then plan a rollback if it is the version I want.
evals.expected_output: Routes the exact article, saved-version inspection, comparison, and rollback plan to fini-api-knowledge rather than treating article evidence as a Conversations workflow.
assertions: Routes current article, history, and exact-version reads to fini-api-knowledge
Does not route article content or version history to fini-api-conversations
Keeps exact-version inspection read-only
Treats rollback as a separate live mutation against the exact article and numeric version

evals.prompt: Compare our current support bot with unpublished prompt pv_42, KB drafts kd_7 and kd_8, snapshot ks_3, and eligible Rulebook version rv_17 before we publish anything.
evals.expected_output: Routes the request to fini-api-draft-validation for an artifact-free baseline, isolated exact-ID candidates, and an intentional combined candidate with no publication implied.
assertions: Routes the active-versus-unpublished comparison to fini-api-draft-validation
Persists and fetches exact candidate IDs through their owning skills
Tests prompt, knowledge drafts, snapshot, and eligible rule version one dimension at a time
Uses like-for-like fresh conversations and, when using MCP, its markAsTest input without inventing that top-level field on direct REST
Keeps a Test Set separate as post-publish persistent live-agent regression
States that Generate Answer may invoke Actions and creates conversation events
Does not publish any candidate

evals.prompt: Read-only: explain the stored execution trace for this exact Fini response, then audit our current Reply Rules for no reply, internal comment, and direct reply.
evals.expected_output: Routes the exact historical event trace to Conversations and the current workspace Reply Rule audit to Agent Configuration, keeping observed execution evidence separate from current configuration.
assertions: Routes exact event metadata to fini-api-conversations and verifies role=finibot
Routes Reply Rules and Reply Rule fields context to fini-api-agent-configuration
Keeps stored event execution evidence distinct from current workspace Reply Rule configuration
Keeps Reply Rules distinct from intent Rulebooks and Business Rules
Does not use current Reply Rules as conclusive historical execution proof
Does not Replay, Generate Answer, evaluate a Rule, execute an Action, or mutate configuration
